title: Every root mutation reads and hashes the root's whole membership, so its cost grows with the root's history
outcome: Each mutation under a root (decompose, dispose, waive, note, gate, checkpoint) does a validated read of the root's current state and hashes all of its members, so its cost is linear in the root's members and a long-lived root makes every mutation under it slower. Either bound that cost by something that does not grow with closed history, or measure it on the live store with the release build and record why it is accepted.
acceptance: A decision is recorded: either a bounded design (for example an incremental state checksum) filed as follow-up work with its migration or repair consequence named, or an explicit acceptance of linear cost with the member count at which it becomes a problem.
The per-mutation cost of a note, a gate, a decompose and a waive under the live store's largest root is measured with the installed release build and recorded.
